ordinance_area_text: It is hereby declared to be unlawful for any person to do any of the acts set forth in this section within the limits of the facilities and lands located within any public park or parkway or lands used by the county for related purposes within the limits of the county; (1) To carry or discharge any firearms, firecrackers, rockets, torpedoes or fireworks of any kind without written consent of the administrator, with the exception of duly authorized law enforcement officials on official duty and with the exception of persons legally permitted to carry a firearm as a concealed weapon, pursuant to Code of Virginia, § 18.2-308 et seq. as amended, while in compliance with any laws or regulations appertaining to such permit.
method: Rebuilt 2026-11. A full owner search of the county's Vision assessment database (gis.vgsi.com/TazewellCountyVA, owner 'TAZEWELL COUNTY', all result pages) found 242 parcels, 59 of them owned by 'TAZEWELL COUNTY (BD OF SUPERVISORS)'. Each of the 59 parcel cards was read for land use, acreage and outbuildings (picnic shelters, bath houses, restrooms and so on). Parcels were joined by PTM_ID to VGIN statewide parcel geometry (FIPS 51185). Two areas qualify. (1) Cavitt's Creek Park / Lake Witten: county parcels 75-A-1A, 75-A-2A, 75-A-3, 75-A-3A, 75-A-4A (757 Recreation Dr: picnic shelters, cabin, bath house), 74-A-143A, 55-A-27A/27B/27C, 55-A-28B (picnic shelter) and 55-A-28C (Mountain Lake Dr), and 54-A-102/102A, unioned with the DCR Conservation Lands 'Cavitts Creek Park' polygon. (2) Tazewell County Fairgrounds: county parcel 94A8A-23 (17.5 ac, Fieldcrest Cir, at the end of Fairground Rd). Its card lists large exhibit/outbuildings, a 3,360 sq ft picnic shelter, a restroom, 47,000 sq ft of paving, a sign and a shop, and TIGER roads show a loop track inside it. Union with a 5 m closing in a local metric plane, holes under 5000 m2 filled, simplified 1 m, rounded to 1e-5 deg. Script: scratchpad areas-recheck/build.py.
notes: Cavitt's Creek is about 231 acres. The fairgrounds is about 18 acres, 0.6 mi west of the Town of Tazewell. Article II of Ch. 14 (Sec. 14-32 (32a)) itself refers to 'the county properties generally known as the Tazewell County Fairgrounds', and the county funds fairgrounds repairs (May 2025 Board of Supervisors agenda). The earlier note that the fairgrounds was the privately assessed parcel 94-A-52 (Peery) appears to be wrong: that parcel is the farmland to the south along Fairground Rd. The county-owned 94A8A-23 is the developed fair site. Still, it was not confirmed on the ground or by the county that every fair-use area lies inside this one parcel. None of the other 46 Board of Supervisors parcels looks like a park: they are the courthouse and office complex in downtown Tazewell, the Lynn Hollow landfill and convenience sites, the airport area, small vacant lots and community or office buildings. Parcels held by the PSA, the School Board, the IDA and the Airport Authority were not treated as park land. School grounds may have their own state-law firearm restrictions, which are not part of this area. Town parks (Lotito Park, Lincolnshire Park and others) belong to towns, not the county, and are excluded. A park the county leases rather than owns would not appear in an owner search. The ordinance also covers carrying firearms (with exceptions), not only discharge.
